clue.text: Have the effrontery to show one a way to dance

parts.note: gall is cheek or effrontery
the Roman numeral for one is I
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone bold enough to show a stranger how to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have the' and 'to show' only link the pieces. The galliard was a lively Renaissance court dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A galliard is a lively sixteenth-century court dance in triple time.

clue.text: Struggle to give the king fruit

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: A tussle to hand the monarch some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple is to wrestle or struggle with someone.

clue.text: Saul's diet produces languor

indicators.note: the letters of Saul's diet produce a fresh word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A biblical king's restricted eating leaves him listless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces' signals an anagram of SAULS DIET; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is weariness and lack of energy, a near synonym of languor.

clue.text: Second pressing

definitions.meaning: a moment, a very short time

explanation.definitionFit: Both a split-second moment and an urgent, immediate need share this word.

clue.text: Note parent is half-hearted and more aloof

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the heart of the word for parent is two letters, and half of that heart is lost

parts.note: a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: A parent who is lukewarm about things and rather distant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one of the two central letters, the H of TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Remoter is the comparative of remote, meaning more distant or standoffish.

clue.text: indian father's in pain

indicators.note: the clue says the father sits inside the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a pain
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A Native American's father is suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people, so a member is an Indian in the old usage.

clue.text: A way to act in the capital where you can see the stars

definitions.text: where you can see the stars

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: the act goes inside the capital city

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
to do is to act

explanation.surface: Making a stage appearance in the capital, the place to spot celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the stars' suggests celebrities or an observatory; it is a sports stadium with a dome where star players appear.
explanation.definitionFit: The Astrodome in Houston was a domed stadium where sporting stars performed; an astrodome is also a domed observation window on aircraft.

clue.text: Like certain knights in conversation with horseman

definitions.meaning: spoken aloud, knights cannot be told from nights, giving the tales of a thousand and one nights
a desert rider from the Arab world

explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, Arabian Knights and Arabian Nights cannot be told apart; 'with' just links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabian Nights are famous tales, and a desert horseman of Arabia is an Arabian.

clue.text: Ratlike creature often seen at the wheel

definitions.text: Ratlike creature often seen at the wheel

parts.words: Ratlike creature often seen at the wheel
parts.note: suggests a rodent driving, but the wheel is the exercise wheel in a pet's cage

explanation.walkthrough: 'At the wheel' suggests driving; the pet rodent runs in an exercise wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pet rodent famous for running endlessly in a cage wheel.

clue.text: Ship's crew included in property valuation

indicators.note: the ship and crew are taken inside the word for property

parts.note: an asset is a piece of property
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
a crew is made up of men

explanation.surface: A ship's crew are counted when a property is valued.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is an evaluation, such as a valuation of property for tax.

clue.text: A jolly unknown host

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
in algebra Y stands for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A cheerful stranger acting as host at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective, but it is naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a large multitude, especially of soldiers, so an armed force fits.

clue.text: It's humanitarian to halt ship in port for repairs

indicators.note: something taken in for repairs gets put back together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A kindly gesture: stopping a ship in harbour so it can be mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for repairs' signals an anagram of HALT SHIP IN PORT, all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A philanthropist is a person devoted to human welfare, a humanitarian.

clue.text: Hot line Goodfellow spent 40 minutes on?

definitions.meaning: an imaginary circle round the hottest part of the globe
Robin Goodfellow is Puck, who in A Midsummer Night's Dream promises to put a girdle round the earth in forty minutes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot line' sounds like a telephone link; it is a line on the map where it is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The great circle around the earth's middle is the warmest latitude, and Puck's girdle around the globe would follow such a line.

clue.text: More than one offering to put oil on bats when new

indicators.note: the letters are made new, put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Instructions for oiling a new cricket bat as a ritual offering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when new' signals an anagram of OIL ON BATS. British cricket bats are oiled with linseed oil when new.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblations are things presented to God, offerings, and the plural matches more than one.

clue.text: Establish a line in the plant

parts.note: to found something is to establish it
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Setting up a production line in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundry is a works where metal is cast, an industrial plant.

clue.text: Rescuer gives animal an organ transplant?

indicators.note: the organ is planted into the middle of the animal, as in surgery

parts.note: a deer is an animal
the liver is an organ

explanation.surface: A vet saves an animal by giving it a new organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliverer is one who saves or frees others, a rescuer.

clue.text: This isle of stone

definitions.meaning: the ... Isle is a poetic name for Ireland, so this word goes with isle

explanation.walkthrough: The Emerald Isle is Ireland, named for its green fields.
explanation.definitionFit: The green gem beryl gives its name to Ireland's nickname, so the word fits both a precious stone and that isle.

clue.text: Pack up — the monarch has nearly finished in the tent

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ram is to pack or cram

indicators.note: the word is finished all but its last letter

parts.note: a queen is a monarch

explanation.surface: Time to strike camp: the queen's work is nearly done in the tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RAM to MAR; 'nearly finished' cuts the last letter from QUEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large tent used for parties and shows.

clue.text: This soldier is a habitue

definitions.meaning: a soldier in the standing professional army
a frequent customer of a place

explanation.definitionFit: A professional, full-time soldier and a frequent visitor to a pub or shop share the word.

clue.text: Hounds that track blackbirds?

parts.note: small hunting dogs that track game, with a nod to the Beatles, whose track Blackbird swaps one letter of their name

explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints no letter count. 'Track' as a song recalls the Beatles' Blackbird, one letter off the hunting dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Beagles are small scent hounds bred to track hares.

clue.text: Show of boldness causing endless Indian trouble

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Bluster that stirs up endless strife among Native Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a bold or swaggering display intended to impress.

clue.text: The cockney's bald and stuffy

indicators.note: a London cockney drops the initial H sound

parts.note: a bald head is hairless

explanation.surface: A Londoner who is bald and rather pompous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cockney's' drops the H at the front, as a cockney speaker would.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffy room lacks fresh air, so it is close and without ventilation.

clue.text: Came to an agreement and paid

definitions.meaning: reached a deal or resolved a dispute

explanation.definitionFit: To settle is both to resolve a dispute and to pay off what is owed.

clue.text: In good condition — OK for a pot-stand

parts.note: OK means right or correct
as can mean for, in the role of
a trivet is a three-legged stand for a pot

explanation.surface: Something quite fine to use as a stand for a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom means perfectly well; the trivet was steady on its three legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in perfect health or order, a stable three-legged stand being the image.

clue.text: Nonsensical edict?

parts.note: combines the slang sense of rubbish talk with a formal papal decree

explanation.definitionFit: A papal decree is called a bull, and bull is also slang for nonsense.

clue.text: Hard to lace, perhaps, having several sides

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A shoe or corset that is difficult to tie up from any angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals an anagram of HARD TO LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An octahedral solid has eight faces, so it has several sides.

clue.text: Bits of man-made bristle found here

indicators.note: the letters are sitting inside the words man-made bristle, so they are found there

explanation.surface: Scraps of synthetic bristle lying about from a broom.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered fragments or rubbish, loose bits left over.

clue.text: Given a hair cut, so turned mutinous

indicators.note: mutinous letters rebel and fall out of their places

explanation.surface: A monk shorn and then turned rebellious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutinous' signals an anagram of SO TURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk, so a tonsured head has had that cut.
